rationale: The availability experiment for the replay-completion question has been executed (receipt ebb3bb9fa26547f790129eea909d1d5a): the witness at parsed event 11 shows a group that commits with two members live and loses that ability after one further stop when the third member never returned from NewRaft, and the flag-off control holds at event 14. The member loss is therefore measured rather than argued, so this batch replaces the account with one that cites all three receipts.

interpretations.joint_history: All three receipts are executions of fixed experiments for this investigation on the same captured source revision, in separate workspaces with no shared mutable state. Receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f and its revision e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 use one harness whose cases differ only in Config.MaxAppendEntries and the committed range; e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 re-runs the original 9000-entry pair unchanged, so its operands are directly comparable with the earlier receipt. Receipt ebb3bb9fa26547f790129eea909d1d5a uses a different harness that exercises the same mechanism in a three-voter group at the same MaxAppendEntries 16 and the same measured bound (event 9: 3000 replayed entries, 188 batches; event 10: no return from NewRaft), and adds the availability consequence the single-voter prefixes could not show. No receipt depends on another's runtime state, and the phase of the blocked case is corroborated in each by a stack sample naming the replay frames.
interpretations.rationale: Mechanism. With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs set, NewRaft reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs with it before starting any background goroutine (api.go:723-754). processLogs delivers batches of at most config.MaxAppendEntries commit tuples through a select whose only other case is shutdownCh (raft.go:1302-1312), fsmMutateCh is created with capacity 128 (api.go:560), and its only consumer runFSM is started by api.go:636-638 after the replay returns, so ceil((commitIndex - lastApplied)/MaxAppendEntries) sends beyond 128 wait for a consumer that cannot exist until the blocked call finishes, with no timeout. Block. Receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f restarts a single-voter prefix holding 9001 committed entries above an absent snapshot (event 16, 141 batches at MaxAppendEntries 64); the flag-on restart admitted by event 17 did not return within 8000ms (event 18) with the stack naming processLogs at raft.go:1346 called from restoreFromCommittedLogs at api.go:753 called from NewRaft, while the flag-off restart of the same shape returned in 5ms (event 21) and became leader (event 22); receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 reproduces both with return in 1ms. Bound. The revision of that harness adds a flag-on pair at MaxAppendEntries 16: 1501 replayed entries, 94 batches, returned in 0ms (event 25, comparison holds); 3001 entries, 188 batches, did not return (event 29, comparison violated, stack naming the same frames). Same flag, same batch size, same stores, only the replay volume differs, so the boundary sits between 94 and 128 batches, that is at 128 * MaxAppendEntries entries - 2048 at 16 and 8192 at the default 64. Availability. Receipt ebb3bb9fa26547f790129eea909d1d5a builds three voters at MaxAppendEntries 16, commits 3000 commands through a leader that is not A (event 9: A's staged commit index 3000, snapshot index 0, 188 batches), and restarts A in a goroutine. With the flag on the call did not return within 8000ms and the stack sample again names the replay frames (event 10), while the group kept committing with two members live (event 11: commit_while_two_live_ok true); stopping the member that is neither the leader nor A then left a single live member and the next command failed with 'leadership lost while committing log' (event 11: commit_after_stop_ok false). With the flag off, the same prefix and the same stop left the pair {leader, A} live and the command succeeded (events 13, 14: new_raft_returned true in 0ms, commit_after_stop_ok true). The only difference between the two cases is whether the restarted member came back, so the lost commit is attributable to the member that never started. Defect account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft cannot complete startup whenever the committed log it replays needs more than 128 batches, that is more than 128*MaxAppendEntries entries above the restored snapshot index; at the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 that is 8192 entries and it is proportionally smaller for any smaller legal value, as measured at 16. The failure is a startup liveness failure: the node never begins participating, so a single-voter group stays down, and in a larger group the cluster keeps running on the remaining members with proportionally less fault tolerance - as observed, one member that could have started plus one deliberate stop is enough to make the group unable to commit. The pending operations the leader had accepted are answered with ErrLeadershipLost once it steps down (raft.go:508-528), which is the error text recorded in the witness.

knowledge.assertion: Each batch is delivered with a select between a send on fsmMutateCh and shutdownCh, so a full channel with no consumer waits indefinitely.
fsmMutateCh has capacity 128 and its consumer runFSM starts only after the startup replay returns.
The replay range above the snapshot sets the batch count, and the automatic snapshot cadence is the only bound on that range in a default deployment.
With the flag on, lastApplied is set to the persisted commit index before the replay, so the replay range spans the committed log above the snapshot.
The tracked latest configuration feeds quorumSize and the vote-admission checks, which is why a member that never starts is simply absent from every future majority.

counterevidence: The block itself is evidenced by non-return within an 8000ms window plus one stack sample per blocked case (events 18, 29 and 10). The permanence argument does not rest on those samples: the source shows no timeout, a single consumer started only after the blocked call returns, and an escape requiring an object the caller has not received. The flag-off controls return in 0, 1 and 5 ms across the receipts (events 21, 25 and 13).

The measured bound comes from two batch sizes and one replay per side, so the boundary is bracketed between 94 and 128 batches rather than binary-searched; the arithmetic form of the bound is supported by the source, and a registration between the two would be needed to place the edge exactly.

With the default SnapshotThreshold of 8192 equal to the default bound, a default node blocks only when the committed range above its newest snapshot exceeds 8192; every case here raised SnapshotThreshold, a legal Config field, so how readily a default deployment crosses the bound is not measured.

The availability case contains a deliberate second stop, so what it shows is the loss of the group's fault-tolerance margin rather than an outage in an untouched cluster; the control with the replay disabled performs the same stop and still commits, which is what attributes the loss to the member that did not return.

In the flag-on case the surviving leader's command failed with 'leadership lost while committing log', which is the leader stepping down and failing its pending operations rather than a defect of its own. The same apply succeeded while two members were live (event 11, commit_while_two_live_ok true) and succeeded after the same stop in the control (event 14), so the failure is attributable to the missing quorum.

The blocked NewRaft call is abandoned in a separate goroutine so the test can complete; that is a harness choice, not a repair, and the harness never observes the process-level consequence of a caller that waits forever.
limitations: All nodes are in-memory transports and stores in one process with a test commit-tracking store; no production store and no process-level restart are exercised, and the confined goroutine is the only trace of the real caller's hang.
The availability case uses one prefix shape, one batch size (16) and one extra stop, and both observation windows are 8000ms for the restart and 3000ms for the applies.
Schedule variation is limited: the original pair appears in two receipts, the bound pair and the availability pair in one each, and the blocked state is sampled once per blocked case.
The bound's dependence on the caller-side store is assumed rather than verified: the replay range comes from the stored commit index, whose durability contract belongs to the LogStore implementation.
